newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asian funds manager bullish on greater China.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asian funds manager bullish on greater China.

text.p: Australian institutional investor National Mutual Holdings sketched on Monday a bullish short-term investment outlook for most of Asia's tiger economies, but sounded caution on Thailand and South Korea.

The group's Hong Kong-based Asian funds management arm, which has A$1.9 billion (US$1.5 billion) under management, outlined its investment assumptions at a luncheon held in Melbourne to market a new wholesale Asian growth fund.

"The message we want to tell is that if you buy Asia now, it will be for a very reasonable price. You are not coming in at the top," said Matthew Lee, senior funds manager and a director of National Mutual Funds Management (Asia) Ltd (NMFM Asia).
NMFM Asia is overweight or neutral in five of its eight main equity investment markets of Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan and South Korea.
It is underweight in Singaporean, Thai and South Korean stock markets, but Lee expressed optimism about a pick in the Singapore, citing signs of a pick-up in the electronics sector.
"We are expecting Singapore's economy to bottom out this year and gradually recover in 1997," Lee said.
But NMFM Asia remains negative on the Bangkok and Seoul stock markets, he added.
"As far as the (Thai) stock market is concerned, I think a near-term concern will be political stability," he said.
"I think there will be a new coalition government being formed. The test will be whether this new coalition government will be sustained over the next six to nine-month period."
On South Korea, Lee said: "We are still quite negative.

"The country's stock market performance is historically strongly consolidated with its trade performance and we're not expecting the Korean trade picture to improve over the next six months," Lee said.
